statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail remains in the low band while event, rates and geopolitical stress remain extreme.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains below WATCH; the main conditional checkpoints are the 12:30 UTC U.S. data cluster, the cash open and the multi-stage FOMC sequence.
headline: Tail remains low as Nasdaq-100 futures firm modestly ahead of a high-stress U.S. data and FOMC session
body: Fresh reporting shows Nasdaq-100 futures modestly higher while oil eases and Treasury yields remain elevated. Direct live NQ retracement structure is not independently verified, so current Tail remains low despite extreme macro, policy and geopolitical stress.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail ranged from 17% to 23%. WATCH covered parts of the September 15 U.S. session, while Tail returned to the low band from 20:00 UTC and remained low through 10:00 UTC on September 16.
outlookSummary: Conditional Tail rises to WATCH around the 12:30 UTC releases, cash open and the multi-stage FOMC sequence, peaking at 24%. A higher band requires observed persistent one-way structure, failed retracements or a credible delayed second leg.

forecast.analysis: Latest verified premarket reporting had Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.3% higher, with technology mixed, oil lower and Treasury yields still elevated. Live NQ pullback depth is not independently verified, so Tail remains low.
drivers: Nasdaq-100 futures about 0.3% higher in latest verified premarket report
Oil is easing while Treasury yields remain elevated

forecast.analysis: Retail Sales and import/export prices arrive at 12:30 UTC. WATCH reflects conditional event-path risk; meaningful post-release retracements would argue against a persistent Tail path.
drivers: 12:30 UTC Retail Sales and import/export prices

forecast.analysis: The first post-data hour leads into the 13:30 UTC cash open. WATCH assumes opening-auction behavior is unobserved; repeated extension after failed pullbacks would be the adverse checkpoint.
Early cash trade overlaps the 14:00 UTC inventories release. Tail stays at WATCH's upper edge unless the opening move broadens into persistent, shallow-pullback continuation.
By late morning, Tail can ease if the opening impulse retraces normally. It stays on WATCH while post-data directional efficiency and cross-asset alignment remain unresolved.
Midday WATCH sits at its floor with the FOMC still ahead. Two-way trade and deeper retracements would be stabilizing; renewed one-way efficiency would keep risk elevated.
Risk rises into the 17:45 UTC danger-window start. A pre-decision extension that holds near an extreme would be the condition for more concern.
The 18:00 UTC FOMC decision and 18:30 press conference create peak event stress. Tail remains WATCH unless repricing becomes persistently one-way with failed retracements.

forecast.analysis: Press-conference and Q&A repricing remain the key checkpoint. Tail is capped at WATCH absent observed alignment between NQ persistence, yields and weak retracement quality.
The delayed second-leg window is still active. Tail stays WATCH while the market tests whether the policy move extends or mean reversion reasserts itself.
After the main policy window, conditional Tail begins to decline if extremes stop extending. Persistent late-session directional efficiency would delay that normalization.
Late-session risk remains elevated but below the FOMC peak. A stable close-side structure with ordinary pullbacks would reduce delayed-repricing concern.
After U.S. cash hours, Tail returns to low under the assumption that no persistent second leg has formed. Any unresolved cross-asset dislocation would invalidate that easing.
drivers: Overnight transition after U.S. cash close
Whether a delayed second leg remains unresolved

forecast.analysis: Early overnight risk is lower once the main FOMC transmission window passes; post-decision rate and equity stabilization remain the key conditional check.
Overnight Tail stays low if the Asian handoff is orderly and U.S. post-FOMC extremes are not extended. Fresh directional discontinuity would raise the score.
Low Tail assumes no renewed one-way impulse during the Asian session. Stress remains high because post-FOMC repricing and elevated energy and rate levels can still produce volatility.
Risk remains low if overnight price discovery stays two-sided. A sharp cross-asset alignment after the policy decision would be the main invalidation.
drivers: Cross-asset alignment after the policy decision

forecast.analysis: Late-Asia conditions are expected to be quieter, but the assessment remains conditional on no fresh continuation from U.S. policy repricing.
The Europe-open transition modestly raises conditional risk because liquidity and rates can reprice the prior U.S. move. Tail stays low without persistent extension.
drivers: Rates response to prior U.S. policy repricing

forecast.analysis: European participation provides a fresh check on post-FOMC direction. Conflicting rates and equity signals would favor a low-Tail, mixed regime.
Tail remains low if European trade absorbs the prior policy move with normal pullbacks. Renewed session-extreme holding would increase risk.
drivers: Session-extreme holding as an adverse checkpoint

forecast.analysis: Late-European morning risk is still dominated by post-FOMC digestion rather than a verified one-way path. Stress stays high while Tail remains low.
The U.S. premarket handoff begins to matter again. Tail edges higher only as a conditional allowance for renewed directional alignment, not as an observed move.
Approaching the next U.S. data window, stress rises while Tail remains low. Any higher band would require live evidence of persistent extension or failed retracements.
drivers: Live extension and failed retracements would raise Tail

forecastDetail.comment: Current Tail stays low because verified premarket evidence is mixed and live NQ pullback structure is unavailable.
12:30 UTC data lift conditional Tail to WATCH; actual post-release retracement quality remains the key checkpoint.
The cash-open hour stays WATCH because opening-auction continuation and failed pullbacks are not yet observed.
Early cash trade remains WATCH around inventories; persistence, not event existence, would justify escalation.
Late-morning WATCH can ease with normal retracements; unresolved directional efficiency keeps stress extreme.
Midday WATCH sits at its floor while the FOMC remains ahead; two-way trade would be stabilizing.
